Migration_Intent: The Customer intends to migrate their existing [Source DWH] data warehouse, currently hosted on [Source Cloud Environment], to the [Target Cloud] data platform.

The Customer is planning to migrate its current [Source DWH] environment along with its associated workloads to a cost-effective unified modern data warehouse in the [Target Cloud] Platform with no changes in the data model and is seeking subject matter experts to help fulfill its objectives.
Application_Repointing: Along with the migration, the Customer intends to repoint (change the configuration to work with the target platform) dependent up- and down-stream applications to the [Target Cloud] data platform.
Specifically, this includes [ETL/ELT Tool] (source as [Data Lake/Storage]) and [Reporting/BI Tool].
Cloud_Initiatives: The Customer is currently building their Cloud infrastructure and data and AI/BI platform foundation as part of their broader Cloud Shift Initiative.
Business_Value_and_Strategic_Alignment: Define measurable Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) reduction targets post-migration.
Establish baseline metrics for query performance improvements and concurrency scaling.
Link the migration objectives directly to the broader enterprise data strategy (e.g., enabling advanced AI/ML capabilities, real-time analytics, data mesh architecture).

Source_Systems: [File Transfer Protocol / 3rd Party File Based System]

Migration_Strategy: Provide guidance on establishing a foundational and Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDWH)-specific [Target Cloud] data platform architecture.
Encompass crucial aspects such as controls, networking, access, security, and deployment artifacts, to create a tailored EDWH-fit cloud environment.
Facilitate the migration of the existing [Source DWH] enterprise data warehouse to [Target DWH].
The solution is 'lift-and-shift', preserving the logical structure of the current environment.

Specifically cover: (i) fully migrated [Source DWH] data warehouse to [Target Cloud]; (ii) [Reporting Tool] consumption layer pointing to a defined target Cloud; (iii) Revised downstream interface with the [Target Cloud] data warehouse; (iv) Requirements for dependent technical and infrastructure components; (v) Reference mapping between [Source DWH] artifacts and relevant [Target Cloud] equivalents.

Recommendations: Modernization strategy (Milestone and Approach), Modernization plan, Testing Strategy, Provide guidance on a high-level design for a clean room in [Target Cloud].

Defect_Categories_and_Resolution: P 1 - Critical: Preventing or severely limiting the use of important functionalities or essential part thereof. There is no workaround.

P 2 - Major: Considerably limiting the use of important functionalities or essential parts thereof. Example: Inaccurate Data Transformation leading to temporary corrective action; Partial functionality in the Consumption Layer lacking full data field and security access. There is a workaround.
P 3 - Minor: The use of the Work result is impaired only insignificantly or not at all. Example: Typing errors, formatting errors, incomplete in-line code documentation. There is a workaround.
Non-Material Defects (Category P3 and up to a specific number of P2 defects) do not entitle Customer to refuse Acceptance.
Security_Compliance_and_Lineage_Parity: Target environment matches or exceeds the legacy [Source DWH] environment's Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Row-Level, and Column-Level security policies.
Data tracking and lineage features successfully map 100% of critical data elements post-migration to tools like [Data Catalog Tool].

4.1 Project Assumptions: Migration strategy will be lift and shift migration with minimal or no data model changes.
Due to the current health/geography-related restrictions, a remote delivery model is assumed to deliver the project.
For this project code exchange will occur through the Customer's version control repository (e.g., GIT).
Deployment into the Production environment will be done by the Customer team.
All documents and communication related to the project, agreement and business will be in English.
Contractor will align all Customer communication with Professional Services beforehand.
Contractor is not responsible for any infrastructure-related costs, such as egress charges associated with data movement via ETL processes.
Any changes to the codebase and Jobs of the peripheral systems will be handled by the Customer team.
The current estimate is the extent of the services provided. Any change requests resulting in changes in scope and/or timeline due to delays will be estimated separately.
Mutually agreed working hours and timezone overlap established for offshore/onshore coordination.
4.2 Technical Assumptions: The Cloud foundation and projects are already in place and any gaps identified by the Contractor team during project execution will be filled by Customer Team.
Any upgrades/ patching/ changes of [Message Broker] and other source systems will not require changes in the Data/ file format and interfaces.
No change in the structures of existing elements/ tags in XML/ JSON.
Customer team will freeze the code for a mutually agreed period of [Source DWH]/[Source Cloud] Production codes covering all end-to-end Pipelines before the start of the migration sprints.
The complete list of peripheral systems included as part of the scope is defined.
All the peripheral systems will be running on their existing infrastructure.
The frequency and timing of outbound feeds will be similar to the legacy environment.
Encryption or decryption of data is not included beyond publicly available [Source DWH] and [Target Cloud] encryption/decryption functionality.
Any data not captured in volumetrics or in non-production environments is excluded as migration to avoid costs in ingress, egress scenarios.
The scope of [ETL Tool] is limited to specific pre-defined pipelines.
API rate limits on peripheral systems will not throttle the target DWH extraction/loading processes beyond modeled thresholds.
Source systems will support Change Data Capture (CDC) tracking without exceeding mutually agreed latency SLAs during incremental validation phases.
4.3 Customer Dependencies: Customer will establish the Cloud Foundation (Organization, parent folder structure, Billing Accounts, Cloud Identity Provider, IAM roles).
Customer to provide Contractor with necessary access within a mutually agreed timeframe after a written request (Administrative access, Network Topology, Security).
Customer relies on a dedicated Interconnect between legacy cloud, on-prem, and target cloud. This configuration shall be performed by the Customer.
Acknowledge and accept possible implications on data latency, extra computational capacity, and networking charges resulting from cross-cloud interconnects.
Customer will perform the Re-Hosting of relevant upstream/downstream components (e.g., [ETL Tool] Data Plane) before the specified project month.
Provide 3rd party files in the [Cloud Storage] bucket as per agreed planned dates.
Setup connectivity and configuration between the in-scope Reporting tools to [Target Cloud] [X] days before applicable sprint development starts.
